title: Dulce de Leche Icebox Cake
changes_from_base: Chocolate sandwich biscuits stood upright in a loaf tin between plain and dulce de leche whipped creams, then frozen, instead of sponge and ice cream.
summary: Rows of chocolate biscuits stand upright between swirls of plain and dulce-de-leche whipped cream, creating a striking striped slice when cut.
equipment: stand mixer or hand mixer with whisk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Line
steps.text: Line the loaf tin with a double layer of cling film, leaving plenty of overhang.

steps.title: Whip
steps.text: Whip the 360 ml double cream, 240 ml crème fraîche and ½ tsp fine sea salt on medium-high to stiff peaks, 3-5 min.

steps.title: Split
steps.text: Move 480 ml of the cream to another bowl and stir in 2 tbsp caster sugar, then beat the 80 ml dulce de leche into the rest for 1-2 min until it reaches stiff peaks, and taste for salt.

steps.title: Base
steps.text: Flick small dollops of both creams over the base and sides of the tin and smooth to 6 mm, then lay 8 of the 40 biscuits on the base and press in, followed by more dollops smoothed level.

steps.title: Stand
steps.text: Stand a row of biscuits upright along one long side, spoon cream onto biscuits alternating flavours and press them upright against the row to fill the tin.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: Tap the tin to settle the layers, cover with the last of the cream and smooth the top.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Wrap and freeze for at least 6 h; the cake keeps for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Invert the cake, peel off the film and slice with a serrated knife.

tips: Whip the cream mixtures to firm, stiff peaks so the upright biscuit rows hold their shape.
Work quickly once the creams are split so they do not soften before assembly.
Freeze for the full time so the cake slices cleanly with a serrated knife.
storage: Keeps well wrapped in the freezer for up to 1 month.
